A_target.statement:
Let $p, q > 1$ with $\dfrac 1 p + \dfrac 1 q = 1$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \sum_i \size {a_i b_i} \le \paren {\sum_i \size {a_i}^p}^{1 / p} \paren {\sum_i \size {b_i}^q}^{1 / q}$

B_source.statement:
Let $p, q > 1$ with $\dfrac 1 p + \dfrac 1 q = 1$, and $x, y \ge 0$.
Then:
:$x y \le \dfrac {x^p} p + \dfrac {y^q} q$

object_map.reformulation: Normalize the vectors to unit norm, apply Young's inequality to each coordinate pair, then sum.

validity_conditions: Assume ||a||_p, ||b||_q nonzero (else the inequality is trivial); normalize so both norms are 1.
Apply Young coordinatewise to x=|a_i|, y=|b_i|; summing the right sides gives (1/p)sum|a_i|^p + (1/q)sum|b_i|^q = 1/p + 1/q = 1.
Un-normalizing multiplies both sides by ||a||_p ||b||_q, yielding Holder.
proof_plan:
If either norm is zero the result is trivial.
Otherwise, by homogeneity, reduce to the case $\norm a_p = \norm b_q = 1$.

By [[Young's Inequality for Products]]:
:$\size {a_i} \size {b_i} \le \dfrac {\size {a_i}^p} p + \dfrac {\size {b_i}^q} q$

Summing over $i$:
:$\displaystyle \sum_i \size {a_i b_i} \le \frac 1 p \sum_i \size {a_i}^p + \frac 1 q \sum_i \size {b_i}^q = \frac 1 p + \frac 1 q = 1$

Rescaling by $
orm a_p 
orm b_q$ gives [[Hölder's Inequality for Sums]]:
:$\displaystyle \sum_i \size {a_i b_i} \le 
orm a_p 
orm b_q$
{{qed}}
